title: You survived the flood… but you still have to survive what grows inside your own heart after the storm.
paragraphs: You survived the flood… but you still have to survive what grows inside your own heart after the storm.
Noah stepped out of judgment into mercy.

The sky was clear.
The ground was washed.
The old world was gone.
And still, sin was not.
Genesis 9 says Noah planted a vineyard. Then he drank of the wine and became drunk, and lay uncovered in his tent.
That did not happen in one moment.
That kind of fall rarely does.

First, it was just planting.
Then waiting.
Then tasting.
Then lingering.
Then one more cup.
Then silence.
You know that pattern.
God saw it.
You knew.
The thing you called small was not small because of its size. It was dangerous because of where it was leading you.
“Therefore let anyone who thinks that he stands take heed lest he fall.” 1 Corinthians 10:12
Read that again.
Noah had seen the wrath of God cover the earth. He had heard the screams stop. He had watched judgment rise higher than the mountains. He had been carried by grace in an ark he did not deserve.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
A man can survive judgment and still need daily surrender.
The flood removed the world around Noah, but it did not remove the sin nature within Noah.
That is why you cannot trust yourself without God.

That private compromise.
That secret appetite.
That “I can handle it.”
That place you keep revisiting when nobody is watching.
It is not harmless.
James 1:14-15 says each person is tempted when he is dragged away by his own desire. Then desire gives birth to sin, and sin brings death.
Not suddenly.
Slowly.
Quietly.
Until the tent is open, shame is exposed, and what you thought you controlled is now controlling you.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this is not just about Noah. This is about you.
But Jesus Christ came for exposed sinners.

He did not come because you were strong. He came because you were dead in sin. He carried the judgment you deserved, shed His blood on the cross, rose from the grave, and now calls you to repent and live.
“By grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works.” Ephesians 2:8-9
So do not hide in the tent.
Come into the light.
